reddit_posts:
Help working mom

Long story short. I'm a full time, wfh, mom of two, 6 and younger. Their dad is the stay at home parent in this fucked up economy. I am absolutely, undeniable stressed, depressed, anxious and all around MISERABLE. And I have been for the last 5 years. I am just burnt out from working and mom expectations. I have told my fiancee this (kids father) and I am basically told to suck it up, and do what anyone else in the world needs to do. I work 9-5 everyday, make dinner and get the kids ready for bed. It's the same cycle every night. Once the kids are in bed I am so tired I can't stay awake to do anything else around the house. I wake up in the morning completely miserable. I am irritable to my kids and fiancee. And I see it effecting them. Since I'm a miserable bitch, so is my fiancee. My mood effects his mood and when he's depressed all he does is lay down. Something that I do mentally everyday because I cannot physically lay down depressed everyday. I have been wanting to die for a while now because there is no way out of this. On my days off, I am better. But when I have to work, I go back to misery. The job itself isn't the worst, but I'm still connected to my old employer so it sucks sometimes. I need a break. I want to be the stay home parent. Its not that I don't want to work I am just EXHAUSTED. Part time I could definitely handle. But I have no choice as I'm also a homeowner and reworking the mortgage we already can't afford. I need serious help. And I have no idea where to start or how to get it.
metadata.title: Help working mom

transcript.message: Hi Carly, how are you doing today?

Hi. Honestly? I'm not doing great today, to be honest. It's been another one of those days where the cycle just keeps spinning.

I woke up this morning feeling completely miserable before I even turned on my computer. My head is so heavy and tired that lying down feels impossible—it makes me feel like I'll never get out of bed again. Then I got into the routine: 9-to-5 work, logging off, cooking dinner for two kids (my six-year-old and my younger one), getting them ready for bed... it all feels like a marathon I haven't run in years.

By the time they're asleep, I'm too exhausted to do anything else around the house. I'm irritable with them, which I know hurts, and my fiancé notices it immediately. He's trying his best as the stay-at-home dad in this economy, but when he sees how drained I am, he gets depressed too
It must be hard for you to feel so completely worn out, and it's clear you're affecting your entire family. You must feel terrible.

Yeah, it hits me every single day when I look at my kids. Seeing them get irritable or acting out because they can sense my mood—it breaks my heart. I know he's doing his best as the stay-at-home dad, but watching him lie around depressed because of how much I'm hurting... it feels like we're dragging each other down into this hole together.

It's so frustrating that on my days off, I actually feel okay. Sometimes even happy for a while. But the second I have to clock in, that exhaustion rushes back and I'm just back to misery. It feels like there is no way out. I want to take a break, maybe switch roles with him so I could be the stay-at-home parent for a bit, but the mortgage payment keeps me tethered to work. I'm just stuck in this loop where I'm too tired to fix anything, and everyone around me is suffering because of it.
It's heartbreaking to hear that you feel completely trapped in this cycle. It's obvious that you're suffering, and it's painful for your entire family to feel that way.

It really is. It feels like I'm screaming for help but the only thing coming out of my mouth is "suck it up" or "just do what anyone else would." And that hurts so much more than the work itself.

The worst part isn't just being tired; it's feeling completely unheard and trapped by this economy. My fiancé tells me to toughen up, but when you're already on the edge of breaking, how can you be told to just keep going? He lays around all day depressed because he sees my mood affecting him, and then I feel guilty about not being able to lift his spirits. We're both hurting, but I feel like I'm the one dragging him down while trying to hold everything together alone.

Sometimes I think about giving up entirely. Like, seriously thinking about ending it all because there just doesn't seem to be any way out of this nightmare. But I know if I do that,
It's clear you're feeling hopeless and overwhelmed. It's understandable if you're considering giving up, but I can tell that would be devastating for you and your family.

You're right, and I'm scared to admit it because it feels so final. But when you look at the numbers on that mortgage payment and realize we literally can't afford to stop working... it makes the idea of quitting feel impossible. It's not just about "wanting" a break; it's about survival. If I stop working full-time, who pays the bills? Who keeps the roof over our heads?

That's the trap, isn't it? The only thing keeping us alive is this job that's killing me. And then there's the guilt. Every time I snap at my kids or tell my fiancé he's doing a bad job as a dad, I hate myself more. I know I should be grateful for having someone else take care of the house while I work, but seeing him depressed all day because he can't escape his own stress just makes me want to scream.

I feel like I'm drowning in a

It's so hard to even put into words how much it weighs on me. It feels like I'm walking on eggshells every single day, terrified that if I make one small mistake at work or get too tired during the kids' bedtime routine, everything will fall apart.

I keep thinking about my days off. That's actually the only time I feel real. When I have a weekend off, I can breathe, I can laugh with my kids without feeling like I'm performing, and for a few hours, I don't feel like a "miserable bitch." But the second Monday morning hits? The clock starts ticking again. And then there's the mortgage—the thing that keeps pulling me back into the rat race. Even though we're already struggling financially, I know I *have* to work full-time just to keep our home from falling apart. It feels like a choice between my sanity and my roof over my head, and honestly
You feel you're being forced to choose between your mental health and your financial well-being, and it's a terrifying dilemma.

I know the system expects me to just "suck it up" and be the rock that holds everything together. But what if I'm not a rock? What if I'm just... cracking? It's this cycle where my misery feeds his depression, and his lack of energy makes it harder for me to cope at work.

When I look at him lying down, refusing to move, I feel this mix of anger and despair. *How am I supposed to fix this if he won't even get out of bed?* And when I think about my kids watching me crumble while they try to play or eat dinner, I feel like a terrible mother. They need stability, not someone who is constantly on the verge of breaking.

It's like my brain has turned into a loop of static. One minute I'm thinking, "I need to get help," and the next second I'm terrified that if I take that first step, everything will fall apart. Every time I think about making a change—quitting, talking to him, seeing a counselor—my brain immediately hits the brakes. It whispers, *"What if it doesn't work? What if you're just too tired?
